only be maintained by the deliberate exclusion of disturbing
influences. But that too would be a peace such as the world
gives, since it would be we ourselves who fight to conquer it.
The peace which the word of Jesus promises is the peace of
eternity, which abides with us at the very heart of our inner
disquiet and the storms which beat upon us, just because it
is not our peace but God's peace, which transcends our
tumult and unrest. By this peace we gain the power to face
our inner distresses, so that we do not attempt to impose
silence on them, but rather let them speak out loudly. Thus,
so far as is possible, we are enabled to comfort sorrow and to
soothe pain, and we who know something of the peace of
eternity are thus strengthened to deliver the message of this
peace to the world, and to convey its very spirit to the world.
"Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you. Not
as the world gives, give I to you. Let not your hearts be
troubled, neither let them be afraid." This is the voice of the
love of God who calls us to Himselt, and calls us to come to
Him as He invites us to come to this celebration of the
Lord's Supper.
